thread:
nina-support: heads up — customer Jessica from ACME reports GitHub SSO failing with a 'state_mismatch' after the callback. They say the callback hits our /auth/callback with code+state but then a 302 from our edge modifies the querystring and the app refuses the state.

customer-jessica: repro steps: 1) Click Sign in with GitHub 2) GitHub redirects back to https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?code=OIV...&state=abc123 3) Browser shows a quick 302 to https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?state=abc123&code=OIV... and then our UI shows "state_mismatch". Happens intermittently (2/5 tries). Using Chrome stable.

samir: thanks — can you paste the raw redirect headers / full callback URL when it fails? curious if state gets url-encoded or duplicated. In theory express's req.query should handle either ordering so suspect duplicate params or encoding differences.

customer-jessica: here is what I captured from the network tab (raw Location header):

Location: https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?code=OIV...&state=abc123
--> then server returns 302 Location: https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?state=abc123&code=OIV...

I also saw once: https://app.acme.com/auth/callback?code=OIV...&state=abc123%20 (note trailing %20)

raja: FYI I rolled a small edge-worker change ~2h ago that canonicalizes querystrings and strips trailing slashes. Possible we're normalizing qstring in a way that collapses or reorders params. Deploy details below.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: edge-worker/normalize-qstring @ raja — commit f4c3d2a — deployed at 1715003400.

samir: that lines up timewise. If the worker normalizes by decoding and re-encoding params, whitespace/encoding could turn into an extra empty char or duplicate param. Also if our session stores the state as one form (abc123) and the callback sends abc123%20 or two state params, our strict equality check will fail.

nina-support: customer also mentioned they have a Chrome SSO plugin, but they've repro'd in incognito too. They can test a staging build if we patch.

alex: quick mitigation: make the OAuth callback handler tolerant: parse raw querystring from req.originalUrl and collect all values for state (Array or repeated params) and accept if any normalized value === session.state. Add logging for raw callback url so we can see exact form. Pseudocode:

```js
const raw = req.originalUrl.split('?')[1] || ''
const params = new URLSearchParams(raw)
const states = params.getAll('state').map(s => decodeURIComponent(s).trim())
if (states.includes(sessionState)) { /* ok */ }
```

samir: that sounds good. If we accept any matching state we avoid ordering/canonicalization issues. Also add a metric for state_mismatch to see if rate drops.

raja: I'll roll a small fix to edge-worker to avoid decoding whitespace into an extra char; but agree server should be defensive.

alex: pushing patch to staging now, tests run in CI. Will post staging URL.

deploy-bot: Staging deploy started: support-staging/oauth-fix @ alex — build 789 — started at 1715003900.

samir: once staging is up I'll get Jessica to try. Can you include a curl we can run to simulate the double-redirect?

alex: curl snippet to simulate:

```bash
# simulate initial redirect from GH
echo 'GET /auth/callback?code=OIV123&state=abc123 HTTP/1.1' | nc -q 1 app.staging 80
# then simulate edge rewrite to reorder params (second request)
echo 'GET /auth/callback?state=abc123&code=OIV123 HTTP/1.1' | nc -q 1 app.staging 80
```

customer-jessica: I'm available to test in ~20m, please ping here when staging is ready.

nina-support: marking P1 for now. Please update thread with staging URL and outcome. Thanks :pray:
summary: customer reports intermittent GitHub OAuth 'state_mismatch' after edge rewrite changes querystring order; engineering to patch callback handler to accept any matching state and fix edge-worker canonicalization.
